quarterly_data.signal: THREE-TIER DEAL MODEL made explicit. (1) MID-TERM core AI cloud contracts of one to three years — four landmark deals closed in Q2 with REFLECTION, COHERE, an unnamed scale U.S. Neolab and a large U.S.-based quant trading firm, averaging MORE THAN $1B EACH at a yield of $20-25M PER MEGAWATT, upfront payments covering 50-60% of associated capex and payback under two years. (2) SHORT-DURATION capacity of up to six months for time-boxed needs (large training runs before a model release, RL post-training sprints) on dedicated GB300 clusters, being negotiated at $40-50M PER MEGAWATT 'and sometimes above' — roughly double the mid-term yield; one such deal signed recently. (3) LONG-TERM contracts with investment-grade customers, used primarily to finance the build-out. Management states it COULD SELL ITS ENTIRE 2027 CAPACITY TODAY on mid-term terms but is deliberately choosing NOT TO, retaining capacity for higher-value short-term demand; it has also tactically shortened how far in advance it sells, selling closer to deployment to improve realized pricing.

Customer mix de-concentrating: largest data-center customer fell from 63% to 27% of revenue while enterprise channel hit 28% of revenue (+45% QoQ); more NeoCloud / mid- and small-cloud / enterprise customers driving structural margin improvement (Q3 non-GAAP GM 10.1% vs 6.4%).
